name: ARC
ability_definition: The ability to quickly make sense of, combine, and organize information into meaningful patterns.

task_realism.reasoning: At work, Speed of Closure means quickly making sense of fragmented, noisy real information: spotting a pattern in scattered data, recognizing a partial signal on a monitor, or piecing together incomplete reports. ARC's tasks do require assembling sparse examples into a coherent pattern, which captures the organizing core. But the tasks are abstract, clean, deterministic grid puzzles. They lean toward deliberate inductive rule discovery rather than rapid perceptual or situational closure on messy, degraded input.

evaluation_conditions.reasoning: There is no per-item time or latency limit, even though speed is definitional to this ability. Competition compute budgets constrain total runtime, not the speed of closure. Inputs are noise-free and well-bounded. Three attempts are allowed. There are no stakes, ambiguity, or competing demands. The input distribution is a synthetic puzzle space, unlike workplace information streams.

construct_coverage.reasoning: ARC covers one slice: organizing sparse structured examples into a meaningful rule. It omits the speed dimension entirely. It also omits perceptual closure on obscured or degraded stimuli and closure across real-world modalities such as text, images, audio, and data. Performance reflects abstraction and generalization more than quick closure.

format_match.reasoning: Inputs and outputs are small colored integer grids with exact-match scoring. These are toy artifacts with no counterpart in workplace materials such as charts, documents, images, dashboards, or partial reports. The one resemblance is that the output is an open construction rather than a multiple-choice pick.

transferability_reasoning: ARC probes the 'organize information into meaningful patterns' part of Speed of Closure through few-shot abstract rule induction. It does not test speed at all, and it uses toy grids that bear little resemblance to the fragmented, noisy information workers must quickly make sense of. It is a weak, partial proxy: success on ARC says little about rapid real-world closure.

2020.model_or_system: icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind), a program search over a hand-written domain-specific language (DSL)
2020.metric: percent of private evaluation tasks solved (top-3 attempts)
2020.human_reference: General adult population (typical working adults, no specialist training), since Speed of Closure is a broad perceptual-cognitive ability

2021.model_or_system: Icecuber (Johan Sokrates Wind) - DSL-based brute-force program search
2021.metric: percent of hidden private-test tasks solved (top-3 attempts, Kaggle ARC 2020 protocol)
2021.human_reference: General adult population (ARC tasks need no specialist knowledge; Speed of Closure is a general cognitive ability used across many jobs)

2023.model_or_system: Team SM (Somayyeh Gholami & Mehran Kazeminia) and Team MindsAI (Jack Cole), tied for first
2023.metric: percent of private test-set tasks solved (top-3 attempts per task)
2023.human_reference: General adult population (untrained adults solving novel visual pattern-induction puzzles). No specialist workforce exists for this ability.
